title: Misinterpreting Top-K by Omitting the Tail/Other Bucket
pattern: Displaying only the "Top-K" slow processes or operations in metrics while completely dropping the sum of the remaining category.
why_bad: Dropping the rest of the distribution hides cumulative bottlenecks. For example, 10 million small, fast function calls can collectively consume 50% of total runtime, yet they will never appear in any "Top 5" list, misleading developers into optimizing the wrong areas.
detection: Look for slice truncation or limit clauses (`take(K)`) on sorted metrics without computing a remainder category.
strength: Strong` — truncating the population hides aggregate tail execution overhead.
source: Richard L. Sites - *Understanding Software Dynamics* (2021), Section 11.3, p. 193 / p. 205.
